summary: Intermittent high TTFB and mid-request silence for dedicated tenant due to load-balancer backpressure from large custom metadata headers
description:
Issue summary: Customer Foresight Analytics reports intermittent spikes in time-to-first-byte (TTFB) and complete silence mid-request for long streaming completions. Symptoms started 2026-03-11 and escalated after traffic pattern changes (more tracing/metadata).

Impact: ~2–3% of in-flight streamed completions experience TTFB spikes (from ~200ms baseline to 2–8s) and occasional mid-stream disconnects resulting in 502/504 for user-facing requests. Affects dedicated tenant in prod us-east only. Customer reports degraded UX in their chat product and requested urgent mitigation.

Environment: Dedicated deployment, prod us-east-1, region routing through edge gateway cluster gw-us-east-02, backend pool on serving-runtime nodes pool-d-01. Observed on models: open-llama-13b and redwood-v1-qa.

Steps to reproduce (most reliable):
1) Send a long-completion streaming request (>40s expected) with a large set of custom metadata/tracing headers (~>20KB total) and client that uploads the request body in small slow chunks (~1KB every 100ms).
2) Observe initial handshake completes but first streamed bytes delayed (TTFB spike).
3) In some runs, stream goes silent mid-request and ALB/gateway issues a reset/502 after idle timeout.

Observed logs / signals:
- Edge gateway access logs show multiple requests with large header_size values and many small write events to upstream.
- Proxy (nginx/h2 proxy) error.log: repeated "upstream write timeout" and "client aborted" entries correlated with request ids.
- Serving runtime logs show no obvious CPU/GPU saturation; KV cache warmup patterns normal.
- Tracing headers (x-ctx, x-trace, baggage) grow on the wire when clients re-use connections leading to header table growth on HTTP/2.
- Metrics: 95th TTFB for tenant jumped from 350ms to 3s during incident windows; request count unchanged.

Initial hypothesis: Large aggregated metadata headers + slow client chunking cause the gateway/proxy to buffer writes and coalesce small upstream writes. That buffering combined with write hysteresis in the load balancer leads to delayed flushes (increasing TTFB) and sometimes triggers idle/reset timeouts mid-stream. HTTP/2 header compression (HPACK) growth and per-connection header table behavior exacerbate the issue for long-lived connections.

Actions already taken:
- Support asked customer to test with trimmed headers and faster client chunking; customer confirmed dramatic reduction in failures when headers <8KB.
- SRE performed a canary change on an internal gateway node disabling proxy_buffering for streaming route; preliminary tests reduced TTFB spikes on the canary.
- Ops increased ALB idle timeout from 30s to 90s for the affected pool as a temporary mitigation to reduce mid-stream resets.

Requested next steps:
- Short-term: Keep ALB idle at 90s for affected pool, deploy proxy_buffering=off for streaming endpoints across the cluster, and add an alert for sustained header_size growth per-connection.
- Mid-term: Harden gateway config: increase max header size, tune write buffer thresholds, and add explicit flush behavior for streaming responses.
- Long-term: SDK guidance/validation to compress or truncate tracing baggage and an automated header-size warning in the Console for customers.

Notes: This ticket overlaps with historical proxy/header growth incidents; see linked issues for similar patterns.
investigation_notes:
Timeline: 2026-03-12 09:12 customer ticket -> Support triage. 2026-03-12 11:00 SRE reproduced with internal harness mimicking slow-chunked client and large metadata; confirmed proxy write coalescing increased TTFB. 2026-03-12 14:30 applied canary proxy_buffering=off (gw-us-east-02-a) and saw median TTFB drop to baseline in canary. 2026-03-13 02:00 increased ALB idle timeout to 90s for pool-d-01. Root cause analysis points to interaction between large header frames and proxy buffering/write coalescing on HTTP/2 leading to delayed flush. HPACK table growth makes header frames larger on reconstructions, causing the proxy to spend more cycles and hold writes. No indication of serving-runtime CPU/GPU resource exhaustion.

Evidence: request ids r-20260312-6a1df, r-20260312-6a2b7 included in logs. Sample proxy error lines and ALB logs attached in internal ticket (attachment references).

resolution: Partial mitigation applied: ALB idle timeout increased to 90s for the affected pool and proxy_buffering disabled for streaming route canary. Customer-side header trimming confirmed effective. Permanent fixes planned: update gateway defaults (max header size, write buffer thresholds), route-level buffering exceptions, and Console/SDK guidance. Infra task created (INT-???) to roll changes to all gateways and add header-size alerting. Customer will be notified once config is fully rolled out.
follow_up_actions: Infra task to roll gateway config changes to all clusters and document rollback plan
Add Console alert for per-connection header_size > 16KB sustained for >5 minutes
SDK change to validate and compress tracing/baggage headers by default
Postmortem and runbook update referencing this ticket and linked incidents
